reviews.review:
16 characters all locked by a pay wall. Characters can be unlocked freely if you farm the materials which only have a 6-8% drop rate. However you can beat the game and play it on hard difficulty to increase drop rate to up to 20% chance. After which, these materials need to be crafted / forged together from 4 parts costing around 250,000 in-game credits EACH.

There are 3 base characters that are just too basic to continue playing - even to consider wasting hours on a base character just to beat the game in order to start farming the character you really want.

Its also an South Korean import game, so who knows how much authenticity are we getting from the America version.

Coming in to the game and hearing what it takes to unlock a character just after 2 hours of play, it all feels way to overwhelming to commit to. I dont want to waste 30 hours on a game, just before I can actually start playing it with the character I desired.

Not only repetitive grind, but no guarantee of what you are grinding. First you grind for the weapon, then you grind for an item to reroll stats for that weapon, then you gamble trying to get the stats you want, fail, and grind again. You finally get the stats you want, grind for cores, gamble, repeat. Misions are very few and get repetitive quickly.

Did not like it at all, meaning that the new player experience is dogwater, terrible.
The game:
The "missions" and "fights" if you can even call them that were extremely short for the tutorial, and extremely short after the tutorial - what I think was supposed to be some kind of "story".
The combat felt good-ish, but it was over about 5 seconds before it started, every mission, every group of enemies - deleted in a second.
Even the big bad mech at the end of the tutorial - I shot it ONCE and it triggered a cutscene and exploded - I did not have a chance to even do anything, not even move.

The store(s):
When I got past the tutorial, of course I was overwhelmed by 40000000 currencies, timers, lootboxes, special draws, etc, etc. Basically a cauldron of shop-slop dumped over my screen in what I think was the hub/sanctuary/chill zone.

2/10, maybe even 1/10. It did nothing to engage me, just funnelled me through some linear, 2-second "fights" and then showed me everything I could spend real money on.
It was pretty fun grinding and playing with friends. It's something you can easily pick up here and there. I enjoyed my stay for sure.
